draft.title: Prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells
card: a cell with no nucleus and no membrane-bound organelles. Its DNA lies free in the cytoplasm. Bacteria are prokaryotes.
a cell with a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles. The nucleus holds the DNA inside its own membrane. Animals, plants, fungi and protists are made of eukaryotic cells.
A membrane-bound organelle is a compartment inside a cell that is wrapped in its own membrane. It lets different jobs happen in separate spaces.
Both types of cell have a plasma membrane, cytoplasm, ribosomes and DNA. The difference is whether the DNA and organelles sit inside membranes.
draft.remember: Prokaryotes have no nucleus or membrane-bound organelles. Eukaryotes have both.

a.q: A cell is examined under an electron microscope. Its DNA lies free in the cytoplasm and no organelles have membranes. What type of cell is it?
opts: Prokaryotic, because it has no nucleus
Prokaryotic, because it has no ribosomes
a.why: DNA that lies free, with no membrane-bound organelles, shows a prokaryotic cell. Having DNA does not make a cell eukaryotic, because both types have DNA.
a.clue: Which feature do only eukaryotes have around their DNA?

b.q: Dr Lin finds that a cell from a pond sample has ribosomes, a plasma membrane and DNA inside a nucleus. What can she conclude?
opts: It is eukaryotic, because its DNA is in a nucleus
It is prokaryotic, because it has ribosomes
It is prokaryotic, because it has a plasma membrane
It is eukaryotic, because it has ribosomes
b.why: A nucleus means the cell is eukaryotic. Ribosomes and a plasma membrane are found in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells, so they cannot show which type it is.
b.clue: Only one of these features is found in just one cell type.

a.best: Prokaryotic, because it has no nucleus

b.best: It is eukaryotic, because its DNA is in a nucleus
